messages:
Sabrina Hall: quick sync — postmortem follow-up for NovaHealth onprem peering flap. I pulled together action items from last night's call, please ack and add if I missed anything.

Tim Chen: ack. saw the spike at 02:12 UTC, repeated route withdrawals from their edge.

Kevin Park: +1. Root cause looks like a combination of BGP dampening + MTU mismatch when their edge pushed jumbo frames. Need a reproducible test.

María Gómez: logged customer comms: NovaHealth wants ETA on fix and proof we won't reintroduce traffic leaks. They asked for a timeline for a config change.

Sabrina Hall: action list I have so far (owners/ETA):
- A1: Run deterministic repro in our lab (Tim) — by end of day Tue (1934654290)
- A2: Add alert for asymmetric peering events and add runbook steps (Kevin) — PR by Fri
- A3: Customer config checklist + preflight (María) — share draft tomorrow
- A4: Patch isolation-bug in vpc-peering-agent that allowed stale routes (Eng runtime) — owner TBD, aim next week

Tim Chen: starting lab repro now. I captured the pcap from the incident and a short script to replay. dropping it here: ```bash
tcpreplay -i eth0 capture.pcap
```

Tim Chen: preliminary notes: when we inject 1500->9000 fragmentation the peer drops nlri then BGP session resets after 45s. adding a keepalive tweak avoided immediate reset.

Kevin Park: for A2 — I'll open a tracking ticket and add this alert: "vpc_peering.asymmetry_detected" with tags customer:NovaHealth, severity:warning. Runbook snippet I propose: 
1) check BGP neigh state
2) check if MTU mismatch on interfaces
3) regen route-table, clear stale cached prefixes

oncall-ops: FYI — added scheduled checklist to rotation for this week. I'll take initial oncall validation during Tue daytime window.

Sabrina Hall: on the isolation-bug (A4) I reproduced a race where peering-agent's cache eviction didn't remove learned routes when a session teardown happens mid-reconcile. Repro steps attached in ticket: https://internal/repo/issue/5462 (customer-only link).

Kevin Park: can we get a small patch to force synchronous eviction as a stopgap? If yes I'll approve a hotfix release.

Tim Chen: I can validate hotfix in lab once patch is available. Suggest label hotfix:candidate and smoke tests: BGP flapping, route reconciliation, packet path sanity.

María Gómez: I'll prep the customer note: planned steps, expected impact, rollback plan. Will include proof points (lab run logs + smoke test results).

incident-bot: Incident update recorded: incident-2026-03-22-NovaHealth-peering. SLA impacted: 22m degraded throughput.

Sabrina Hall: blockers?

Kevin Park: need an owner for A4 from eng-runtime. @Tim — can you own triage and nominate runtime eng? If not, I will ping Josh.

Tim Chen: I can lead triage and tag runtime engs. Nominate: Josh Rivera and Anya Patel.

oncall-ops: recorded owner assignments in tracker: A1:Tim, A2:Kevin, A3:María, A4:Tim (triage) + runtime owners. ETA summary posted to tracker.

Sabrina Hall: cool. final ask: can everyone post a 1-line status update in this thread when done with their item so I can close the customer-facing ticket? :thumbsup:

Kevin Park: will post PR link here when A2 is up.

Tim Chen: done with lab repro — reproduced and uploaded logs (link: https://ci.internal/artifacts/peering-repro/1934567890). moving to hotfix testing.

María Gómez: draft customer note sent to #customer-comms for review.

incident-bot: Reminder: follow-up review scheduled in 7 days.
